`as_sexp()` allows to pass objects from Armadillo to R while `as_cpp<>` allows to
pass objects from R to Armadillo. `as_sexp()` allows to convert `mat` to `doubles_matrix<>`
and `imat` to `integers_matrix<>`. `as_cpp<>` allows to convert `doubles_matrix<>` to `mat`
and `integers_matrix<>` to `mat`.

The following functions illustrate this:

```cpp
[[cpp11::register]] SEXP implicit_conversion_double(SEXP x) {
  mat y = as_cpp<mat>(x);
  return as_sexp(y);
}

[[cpp11::register]] SEXP implicit_conversion_int(SEXP x) {
  imat y = as_cpp<imat>(x);
  return as_sexp(y);
}
```

Both of these would work if we pass a matrix $M$ defined in any of the following ways:

```r
M <- matrix(1:4, nrow = 4, ncol = 4)
storage.mode(M)
# > [1] "integer"

implicit_conversion_double(M)

storage.mode(M) <- "double"
implicit_conversion_int(M)
```

It is similar for other Armadillo types, such as `fmat`, `imat` and `umat` with both
`as_sexp()` and `as_cpp<>`.

Besides `SEXP` conversions, `cpp11armadillo` enforces strict types when using
`doubles_matrix<>` and `integers_matrix<>`. For example, the following
function would only work if we pass a matrix of doubles to it:

```cpp
[[cpp11::register]] doubles_matrix<> strict_conversion_double(doubles_matrix<> x) {
  mat y = as_mat(x);
  return as_doubles_matrix(y);
}
```

Otherwise, when passing a matrix of integers to it, we would get an error:

```r
Error: Invalid input type, expected 'double' actual 'integer'
```
